From: Julie Park <julie@fathomlabs.com>

Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commit architecture & token health checklist

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last month. We ran the Q2 export and attached a spend CSV — you can see the growth in inference tokens tied to our new summarization flow (peak at ~3.8M tokens/day for two weeks). Our current reserved commit rolls off on 2028-09-30 and the finance team is asking for a recommended path: either re-up with a flat commit, a stepped commit, or move to a larger burst + trueup cadence.

Key asks:
- Do you have a short checklist you use to map token trajectory to commit structure?
- Any quick bridging options if we need to smooth Q3->Q4 runway?
- Can you share an ROI recap for a staged commit vs. flat re-up (high level is fine)?

I attached the Q2 export (fathom_token_spend_Q2.csv). Happy to jump on a 30-min call next week — Tom (cc) will join from finance.

Thanks,
Julie
Product Ops, Fathom Labs

Attachment: fathom_token_spend_Q2.csv (CSV export, 38KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Julie Park <julie@fathomlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit architecture & token health checklist

Hi Julie — thanks for the export and the context (looks like the new summarization flow drove the Q2 bump). I pulled a quick pass and sketched a pragmatic checklist below; attaching a draft proposal (redwood_commit_proposal_v1.pdf) that maps three commit shapes to your Q3 forecast.

Quick checklist (first pass):
- Validate token mix by API type (generation vs embedding vs rerank) — mismatches change unit economics.
- Identify predictable baselines vs bursty features (summarization appears bursty).
- Latency SLOs & required dedicated lanes — if you need guaranteed p99, that impacts cost.
- Prefetch/prefix caching feasibility for summarization pipelines (could lower sustained token counts).
- Time horizon: 3-month staggered commit vs 12-month flat changes the discount profile.

Bridging options we commonly recommend:
- Stair-step commit (quarterly increase) + small burst credit pool for unexpected spikes.
- Short-term dedicated reserve for peak windows (1-2 months) then true up into staged commit.

I'll put Ben on the thread to validate capacity/latency constraints; Grace will prepare a concise ROI comparison (staged vs flat). If you want, we can run a 30-min alignment next Tue/Wed.

Next steps I can take now:
1) Share the staged commit PDF (attached).
2) Ben to confirm capacity/latency feasibility.
3) Grace to produce a 1-pager ROI recap for finance.

Thanks — Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_commit_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal, 120KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Jul 2028 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit architecture & token health checklist

Priya — I ran the quick capacity calc against the Q2 export. Short summary:
- Sustained baseline (30-day median): ~1.1M tokens/day.
- Peak windows (top 10% of days): up to 3.6–3.9M tokens/day for short bursts.
- If Fathom wants p95/p99 latency guarantees for summarization, we'd recommend a small dedicated pool sized for the 95th percentile and then route the rest to shared capacity.

Attached a short workbook showing runway scenarios and cost deltas (capacity_runway_calc.xlsx).

Operational notes:
- Stair-step commit works well if they can accept quarterly reconciliation; it smooths discounts and reduces near-term cash outlay.
- Burst credits are the fastest remedial lever (non-recurring credit bucket you can consume on spikes).

I'll be available for the Tue call — can present the latency tradeoffs live.

— Ben
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_runway_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet, 56KB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Julie Park <julie@fathomlabs.com>, Tom Carter <tom.c@fathomlabs.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Jul 2028 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit architecture & token health checklist

Julie / Tom — looping you in with a short ROI recap so finance can see the delta quickly. High-level findings (attached PDF):
- Option A (12-month flat re-up): predictable unit price, but ~12–18% higher annual spend vs a staged commit given your Q3->Q4 growth profile.
- Option B (3-quarter stair-step): lowers initial quarter cash outlay and captures expected growth; modeled savings ~9–13% across year 1 vs flat.
- Option C (minimal commit + burst credits + trueup): best for flexibility, smaller committed discount; estimated carry cost in steady state is higher but gives financial agility.

Recommendation for Fathom Labs: start with a 2-step commit (Q4 small bump, Q1 larger) + a $25k burst-credit pool for unexpected spikes. That minimizes short-term cash while protecting p99 requirements via dedicated lanes (Ben's approach).

If that sounds reasonable I can prepare a one-page comparison for your finance team and a templated contract amendment that Priya can share for legal.

Thanks — Grace
Senior GTM Finance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: roi-recap-fathom.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
